intro: When you search for a "reptile vet near me", you're likely looking for a vet who truly understands the special needs of snakes, lizards, tortoises and other reptiles. Reptiles have very specific requirements for temperature, UV lighting, humidity and diet, and many health problems are linked to these factors. Finding a vet with the right knowledge and equipment can make a real difference to your pet's care.
need_heading: What people searching for a reptile vet usually need
need_lead: You want a vet who can properly assess and treat your reptile, and who has the facilities to handle exotic species.
needs: You have a snake that has stopped eating and you're worried it might be due to incorrect temperatures or humidity in its vivarium.
Your lizard is showing signs of lethargy or difficulty shedding, and you suspect the UV lighting or diet might need adjusting.
You need a pre-hibernation check for your tortoise to make sure it is healthy enough to safely go into hibernation.
Your reptile needs a procedure that requires anaesthesia, and you want to know if the practice has experience with reptile anaesthesia.
You're looking for a vet who can provide advice on setting up the right environment for a new reptile you're about to bring home.
context_heading: What to understand about reptile veterinary care
context: Reptile vets have a deep understanding of how temperature, UV lighting, humidity and diet affect the health of snakes, lizards and tortoises. Many common illnesses in reptiles can be traced back to problems with husbandry, so a vet will often ask detailed questions about your setup. It's helpful to note your vivarium temperatures and lighting before the appointment so you can give accurate information.

Before you book, you can check that the vet is registered with the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS) by searching the RCVS register. Some vets hold further qualifications in exotic species or have advanced practitioner status, which you can ask about if your pet has a complex condition. Many practices also participate in the voluntary RCVS Practice Standards Scheme, which inspects premises, equipment and clinical processes.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the species of your reptile, such as a bearded dragon, corn snake or Hermann's tortoise, as different species have different needs.
Describe the symptoms you've noticed, including how long they've been going on and whether they've changed.
Mention the setup of your vivarium, including the temperatures in the basking area and cool end, and the type of UV lighting you use.
Let us know if your reptile has any known health conditions or previous treatments.
Tell us if you need a specific service, such as a pre-hibernation check for a tortoise or a practice that can perform reptile anaesthesia.
Share your location and how far you're willing to travel to see a suitable vet.
questions: Do you have experience treating this species of reptile?
What equipment do you have for reptile imaging and anaesthesia?
Can you advise me on the correct temperature, humidity and UV lighting for my reptile's enclosure?
What should I bring to the appointment, such as photos of the vivarium or a recent faecal sample?
Do you offer pre-hibernation checks for tortoises, and what does that involve?
If my reptile needs a procedure that you don't offer, do you refer to someone who specialises in that area?

faqs.q: How do I find a reptile vet near me?
faqs.a: You can search for local practices that treat reptiles, and check that the vet is registered with the RCVS. iComply can introduce you to a suitable UK professional based on your needs.

faqs.q: What should I do before my reptile's appointment?
faqs.a: Note down the temperatures and lighting in your vivarium, and take photos if possible. Also, write down any changes in behaviour or feeding, as this information helps the vet.

faqs.q: Are all vets able to treat reptiles?
faqs.a: Not all vets have experience with reptiles, as they require special knowledge of husbandry and handling. It's best to ask specifically about their experience with your species.

faqs.q: What is the RCVS and why does it matter?
faqs.a: The RCVS is the regulator for veterinary surgeons in the UK, and all practising vets must be registered with it. You can search the register to confirm a vet's registration before you book.
